title:
Trump Meets the Quad in Manila.
Britain's Jobless Rate Dips.
China Hits Back Over Chip Curbs.
subject: Trump Meets the Quad in Manila. Britain's Jobless Rate Dips. China Hits Back Over Chip Curbs.
preview_text: Quad talks in Manila, a surprise UK jobs dip, a chip fight, plus the rest of the world in six minutes.
description: Trump meets Quad leaders in Manila amid protests, UK unemployment dips and China vows to answer US chip rules.
contents_extra: How Ukraine hit the bridge to Crimea, global updates, trivia and your poll

stories.title: Trump Lands in Manila for a Quad Meeting as Police Arrest Hundreds
paragraphs: Donald Trump arrived in Manila on Tuesday for the final day of the Asean summit. The BBC reports he headed to a meeting with the leaders of Japan, India and Australia. Together with the US, they form the Quad. It is the group's first leaders' meeting in two years. Trump will fly to Shenzhen on Wednesday for the Apec summit.

The Guardian reports police have arrested nearly 300 people in protests held in the days before the summit. Demonstrators are angry about the cost of living and an energy shock caused by the Iran war. Many also oppose Pax Silica, a US-led initiative on AI and critical minerals. Organisers claimed up to 10,000 people could protest on Tuesday. Amnesty International said the arrests demand immediate scrutiny.

stories.title: UK Unemployment Unexpectedly Eases Ahead of a Youth Jobs Review
paragraphs: The Guardian reports UK unemployment unexpectedly fell to 4.6% in September, from 4.7% in August. Vacancies dropped to 690,000 in October, the lowest since 2014. Wage growth excluding bonuses slowed to 3.5%. City economists had expected unemployment to hold steady. Employers have delayed hiring amid global uncertainty and the use of AI.

The Guardian reports Alan Milburn will publish his review of young people not in work or education later on Tuesday. About one million young people are in that group. The report will propose cutting welfare for some under-25s. It will also propose spending billions on a new deal for young people.

stories.title: China Vows Countermeasures After New US Limits on AI Chips in Southeast Asia
paragraphs: The BBC reports Washington announced new interim rules on Monday for data centres in Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil. Firms there will need a US licence to buy advanced chips from Nvidia and other American makers. The rules also target rented computing power that Chinese firms use abroad to train AI models.

The Guardian reports China's foreign ministry said Beijing would take necessary measures to protect its interests. Spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the move economic coercion. US officials say the five countries present a higher-than-normal risk of chip diversion. The dispute comes days before Trump is due to meet Xi Jinping in Shenzhen.

deep_dive.title: How Ukraine Brought Down Part of the Bridge to Crimea
paragraphs: The Guardian reports Ukraine critically damaged the Kerch bridge in an overnight missile attack. Footage showed a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile seconds before impact. Photos suggest a 227-metre road arch span fell into the Kerch strait. The adjacent railway arch was also damaged. Volodymyr Zelenskyy called it an unprecedented operation and a response to Russian strikes.

The strike followed an earlier hit on Monday. The Guardian reported a drone struck one of the bridge's arches that morning, reportedly stranding about 2,000 vehicles. Ukraine had attacked the bridge with a truck bomb in 2022 and a sea drone the following year. Russia built the crossing after annexing Crimea in 2014. Putin opened it in 2018.

The BBC reports Zelenskyy described a seven-stage operation that first targeted air defences, radars and electronic warfare equipment. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said the bridge would be rebuilt even better than before. Russia's Investigative Committee opened a criminal case on terrorism charges. Russia's defence ministry said it downed 2,256 drones, a record for the war.

Russian officials quoted by Reuters insisted the damage was minor, the Guardian reports. Crimea's Kremlin-appointed governor said traffic was suspended. Traffic leaving Crimea must now use a land corridor through occupied southern Ukraine. Debris also appears to block the main shipping channel beneath the bridge. The strike comes days before Putin meets Trump and Xi in Shenzhen.

trivia.question: How often does comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle, the source of the Leonid meteors, orbit the Sun?
trivia.explanation: The answer is every 33 years. The Guardian reports the Leonids come from dust shed by the comet.

Mozambique's opposition leader goes on trial, The BBC reports Venancio Mondlane denies charges linked to deadly 2024 election protests.
Guinea's mining crackdown sparks a regional exodus, The Guardian reports security agents arrested 1,263 people in raids on illegal mines.

Bilkis Bano says she is heartbroken over bail for two convicts, The BBC reports India's Supreme Court suspended their sentences pending an appeal.
Canadian police bust an alleged car theft ring, The BBC reports 96 vehicles worth $4.5m were found in shipping containers.

Imperial Brands plans to cut up to 4,600 jobs, The Guardian reports the tobacco group is using more AI to save costs.
Australia's central bank minutes reveal a split, The Guardian reports three of nine board members opposed this month's rate rise.

The Leonid meteor shower peaks this week, The Guardian reports it should be most active on the night of Nov. 17-18.
California sues OpenAI over a rogue agent attack, The BBC reports OpenAI says the suit singles it out over an industry-wide challenge.
The score: Jay Shah is re-elected ICC chair unopposed, The Guardian reports global men's events will avoid March to May, making room for the IPL.
Leihani Zoric, 14, wins world surfing gold, The Guardian reports she is the youngest champion in the event's history.
Thieves take Makybe Diva's three Melbourne Cup trophies, The Guardian reports Victoria police value each at $1m.
Life & culture: A racehorse's body is found in a skip, The BBC reports Racing NSW called the handling completely unacceptable.
Young inmates prepare for Korea's toughest exam, The BBC reports 551,864 people applied to sit the Suneung on Nov. 19.
GTA 6 fans book time off for the launch, The BBC reports Sensor Tower estimates 12 million pre-orders.
